questions.question: Choose the INCORRECT statement related to monsoon.

options.text: The Southwest Monsoon winds blow over the warm oceans, gather moisture and bring widespread rainfall over the mainland of India.
The intensity and position of the high-pressure area, east of Madagascar, affects the Indian Monsoon.
The difference in pressure over Tahiti (Pacific Ocean), and Darwin in northern Australia (Indian Ocean) is computed to predict the intensity of the monsoons.
The western cyclonic disturbances occur due to withdrawal or the retreat of the monsoon.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The western cyclonic disturbances occur due to withdrawal or the retreat of the monsoon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Western cyclonic disturbances** are weather phenomena typically observed during the winter months.
 
• These disturbances manifest as low-pressure systems originating over the **Mediterranean Sea**. The term "Western" denotes the direction from which they approach India.
 
• These disturbances are characterized by cyclonic storms that develop over land, primarily in the Mediterranean region.
 
• They are often attributed to the temperature gradient resulting from the interaction between warm air from the tropics and cold air from the northern polar regions.
 
• This dynamic interplay of contrasting air masses gives rise to the formation of cyclonic disturbances, impacting weather patterns in regions along their path.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **A monsoon** is traditionally characterized as a seasonal reversing wind accompanied by corresponding shifts in precipitation.
 
• However, its definition has evolved to encompass seasonal alterations in atmospheric circulation and rainfall patterns associated with the annual movement of the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) between its northern and southern limits near the equator.
 
• Typically, the term "monsoon" denotes the wet phase of this seasonal pattern, although there is also a dry phase. Occasionally, it may refer to locally heavy yet short-lived rainfall events.
 
• The major monsoon systems worldwide include the West African, Asian–Australian, North American, and South American monsoons.
 
• These systems play significant roles in shaping regional climates and influencing precipitation patterns across vast geographical areas.

questions.question: The natural vegetation of India is broadly divided into _______ groups.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India** boasts a rich and diverse array of natural vegetation, owing to its varied climatic conditions and geographical features.
 
• This natural vegetation can be broadly categorized into **five main types**:
 
• **Tropical Evergreen Forest: **These dense forests are characterized by lush greenery and high rainfall throughout the year. They are found in regions with warm and humid climates, such as the Western Ghats, northeastern states, and parts of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
• **Tropical Deciduous Forest:** Also known as monsoon forests, these forests experience distinct wet and dry seasons. They shed their leaves during the dry season to conserve water. Tropical deciduous forests are widespread in central and eastern India, including parts of the Deccan Plateau and the Eastern Ghats.
 
• **Thorny Bushes in Deserts:** Found in arid and semi-arid regions, such as the Thar Desert in Rajasthan, these vegetation types are adapted to survive in harsh desert conditions. They consist of drought-resistant plants like cacti and thorny shrubs.
 
• **Mountain Vegetation:** As altitude increases, vegetation varies based on temperature and precipitation. Mountain vegetation includes alpine meadows, coniferous forests, and temperate broadleaf forests. These vegetation types are found in the Himalayan region, including states like Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• **Mangrove Forest:** Mangroves thrive in coastal areas with brackish water and are characterized by salt-tolerant trees and shrubs. They provide important habitats for various marine species and act as natural barriers against coastal erosion. Mangrove forests are found along the coastlines of states like West Bengal, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• India's natural vegetation is shaped by factors such as **soil composition, climate, topography, and precipitation **patterns.
 
• This diverse range of flora and fauna contributes to India's rich biodiversity and ecological significance.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about ‘Loo’ winds in the context of the Indian climate?

options.text: They blow in the winter and rainy season.
They blow in the summer season.
They blow in the winter season.
They blow in the rainy season.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They blow in the summer season.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Loo winds** are hot and dry winds that blow over the plains of North India and Pakistan during the summer season.
 
• The temperature associated with these winds can reach up to **45-50 degrees Celsius**, causing severe heatwaves.
 
• They typically occur between the months of **May and June**.
 
• Exposure to Loo winds can lead to dehydration and heat strokes, making them hazardous to health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The term **'Loo'** is derived from the local language and has been used traditionally to describe these winds.
 
• The regions most affected by Loo winds include the states of **Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh**, and parts of **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• People in these regions often stay indoors during the peak afternoon hours to avoid the adverse effects of the Loo.
 
• Traditional measures to combat the Loo include drinking plenty of water, using cooling drinks like buttermilk, and wearing light-colored, loose-fitting clothes.

questions.question: Which group of the Köppen climate classification system represented by letter code Aw, sometimes called the ‘savannah’ climate, is located just outside the ITCZ near the equator?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tropical wet and dry climate.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Tropical Savanna climate or tropical wet and dry climate is a tropical climate sub-type that corresponds to the Köppen climate bracket orders **Aw( for a dry winter) and As( for a dry summer).**
 
• In substance, a tropical savanna climate tends to either see a lower overall downfall than a tropical thunderstorm climate or have a more pronounced dry season( s).
 
• In tropical savanna climates, the **dry season can come severe, and frequent failure conditions prevail during the course of time.**
 
• Tropical savanna climates frequently feature tree-speckled champaigns due to their blankness, rather than thick jungles.
 
• It's this wide circumstance of altitudinous, coarse lawn( called savanna) that has **led to Aw and As climates frequently being appertained to as the tropical champaign.**
 
• Still, there's some mistrustfulness about whether tropical savanna is climatically convinced. also, pure downs, without trees, are the exception rather than the rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mediterranean climates:**

 
 
• Under the Köppen climate classification, "hot dry-summer" climates (classified as Csa) and "cool dry-summer" climates (classified as Csb) are often referred to as just "Mediterranean".
 
• Under the Köppen climate system, the first letter indicates the climate group (in this case temperate climates). 
 
 
 
• **Marine west coast climate:**
 
 
• marine west coast climate, also called oceanic climate, major climate type of the Köppen classification characterized by equable climates with few extremes of temperature and ample precipitation in all months.
 
• In the Köppen-Geiger-Pohl system, the marine west coast climate is divided into the Cfb and Cfc subtypes.
 
 
 
• **Humid subtropical climates:**
 
 
• the humid subtropical climate, the major climate type of the Köppen classification characterized by relatively high temperatures and evenly distributed precipitation throughout the year.
 
• This climate type is found on the eastern sides of the continents between 20° and 35° N and S latitude. Although the climate is made up of two subtypes (Cfa and Cwa), the Cfa subtype predominates.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true for Indian monsoons?

options.text: Monsoonal rainfall is affected by jet streams
Monsoonal rainfall is the lifeline of Indian agriculture
Himalayas play an important role in monsoonal rainfall
Monsoonal rainfall is not affected by the relief features of the country

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Monsoonal rainfall is not affected by the relief features of the country**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Monsoonal rainfall is not affected by the relief features of the country **is** NOT true for Indian monsoons.**
 
• Monsoonal rainfall in India is indeed influenced by various geographical and atmospheric factors, including relief features such as mountains and plateaus.
 
• **For example, **mountains like the **Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats** influence rainfall distribution through orographic lifting, while coastal areas often experience different rainfall patterns due to their proximity to the sea. Overall, relief features play a crucial role in shaping the spatial distribution of monsoonal rainfall across India.
 
• Therefore, statement 4, which suggests that monsoonal rainfall is not affected by relief features, is not accurate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Monsoonal rainfall is affected by jet streams: **This statement is true. Jet streams, particularly the subtropical westerly jet stream, play a significant role in the onset, intensity, and distribution of monsoonal rainfall in India. Changes in the position and strength of jet streams can influence the behavior of monsoon systems.
 
• **Monsoonal rainfall is the lifeline of Indian agriculture:** This statement is true. Monsoonal rainfall is crucial for agriculture in India, as it provides the majority of the water needed for crop cultivation. The timely arrival and distribution of monsoon rains are essential for crop growth and overall agricultural productivity.
 
• **Himalayas play an important role in monsoonal rainfall:** This statement is true. The Himalayan mountain range acts as a barrier to the moisture-laden monsoon winds coming from the Indian Ocean. As these winds encounter the Himalayas, they are forced to rise, leading to orographic rainfall on the windward side of the mountains. This process significantly contributes to the overall monsoonal rainfall pattern in India.

• **Rajasthan** has the lowest average annual rainfall among the states listed in the options.
 
• Therefore, the correct sequence of Indian states in terms of decreasing average annual rainfall is **Assam > Bihar > Rajasthan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Assam, located in the northeastern part of India, experiences heavy rainfall due to the monsoon and its proximity to the Himalayas.
 
• Bihar, situated in the eastern part of India, receives substantial rainfall, primarily during the monsoon season.
 
• Rajasthan, located in the northwestern part of India, is the driest state in the country, with the Thar Desert occupying a significant portion of its area.
 
• The variation in rainfall is due to geographical and climatic factors unique to each state.

questions.question: Which of the following regions has more seasonal contrast than other regions of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Interiors of India.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** interior part of the India** is characterised by more seasonal contrasts.
 
• The rainfall received by India is largely due to the south-west monsoon winds.
 
• The duration of the monsoon is between** 100 to 120 days.**
 
• The bulk of rainfall received by the country is **concentrated over a few months.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• The** total coastline of India **comprises the mainland coastline and that of the Indian islands. The mainland coastline is 5422.6 km long and the coastline of the islands adds up to 1197 km.

 
 
• The nine states that constitute the mainland coastline are - Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, and West Bengal.
 
• Also, two union territories, Daman and Diu and Puducherry, are a part of the mainland coastline.
 
 
 
• An **Island **on any sea can be classified as a Continental Island and an Oceanic Island. 
 
 
• In India, there are** 1208 islands** but this figure includes all the uninhabited isalnds of the country as well.

questions.question: Which of the following is a temperate marine climate with substantial rainfall in all seasons?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cfb.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Köppen climate region **Cfb is described as the Marine west coast climate **because the climate is set up along the western beachfront of mainlands worldwide.
 
• Its high moisture utmostly characterizes it.
 
• **Cfb = Temperate oceanic climate or tropical upland climate; coldest month averaging above 0 °C( 32 °F)( or −3 °C( 27 °F)), all months with average temperatures below 22 °C(71.6 °F), and at least four months comprising above 10 °C( 50 °F).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Am:** Tropical monsoon climate
 
• **BSh:** Hot semi-arid climate.
 
• **BSk: **Cold semi-arid climate.
